member.name: T:PdfToSvg.FontResolver
member.summary: Resolves which font to be used for text in the SVG, for a given PDF font name.

example.para: The following example will use to convert a PDF to SVG without embedding fonts into the extracted SVG. Instead local fonts assumed to be installed on the client machine are used.

code.title: Using local fonts instead of embedding fonts

example.para: Custom behavior can be achieved by subclassing and implementing the method. Here is a custom implementation using a locally installed Open Sans font.

remarks.para: The font resolver will for each font from the PDF provide a substitute font to be used in the generated SVG. Types of substitute fonts that can be returned:

item.description: A font that is assumed to be installed on the machine viewing the SVG.

Use a provided TrueType, OpenType, WOFF or WOFF2 font. Note that external resources are not allowed in standalone SVG files when displayed in browsers, so if you intend to use external SVG files, you need to return a instance using data URLs only.

Inlines the glyphs from the font as paths and other elements within the SVG. This differs from , which are embedded as font files in the SVG. The inlined glyphs cannot be selected as text in the SVG. Currently only Type 3 fonts can be inlined, but more font types might be supported in the future.

remarks.para: PDF documents store text encoded as character codes, and provide mappings from character codes to font glyphs and Unicode characters. Some documents map multiple character codes to the same Unicode character, giving PdfToSvg.NET a choice. Exporting both character codes as the same Unicode character results in good text representation but potentially visually inaccurate SVG’s. Remapping one of the character codes to another Unicode character ensures visually accurate SVG’s at the cost of inaccurate text representation if text is exported from the SVG.
When exporting text using a , the library will use the Unicode mapping specified by the document, providing more accurate text representation.

When exporting text using a , the library will remap duplicate character codes to characters in the Private Use Areas, making sure the exported SVG’s are visually accurate, but text might appear as a series of question marks, ������, in the SVG markup. If you intend to extract text from the SVG, consider exporting the SVG using local fonts instead.

member.name: T:PdfToSvg.InlinedFont
member.summary: Represents a font whose glyphs are inlined as paths and other elements within the SVG markup.

remarks.para: Objects of this type can be returned from a to indicate how text will be rendered in the generated SVG.

differs from , where the latter embeds fonts as OpenType or WOFF font files in the generated SVG. Side effects from inlining glyphs are that exported text will not be selectable, and that the generated SVG will typically be larger than if the font is embedded as a font file.
Currently only PDF fonts of type 3 can be inlined, but more font types might be supported in the future.
PdfToSvg.NET is able to convert most type 3 fonts to OpenType or WOFF, but a subset of type 3 fonts cannot be converted, e.g., bitmap fonts. is mainly intended for this subset.

summary.para: The easiest way of getting started with PdfToSvg.NET is by installing the NuGet package.
Open a PDF document by calling PdfDocument.Open(). Then use either SaveAsSvg() or ToSvgString() to save each page as SVG.
By default, PdfToSvg.NET will try to extract fonts embedded in the PDF and embed them in the output SVG as data URLs. This behavior can be changed by specifying another .
summary.note: If you parse the XML returned from PdfToSvg.NET, you must preserve space and not add indentation. Otherwise text will not be rendered correctly in the modified markup.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.OpenOptions.Password
member.summary: The password used for opening the PDF. This can be either the user password or the owner password. If the owner password is specified, any usage restrictions are bypassed.

remarks.para: PDF documents have two types of passwords: a user password and an owner password. If the document is encrypted, you will need either the user password or the owner password to be able to open and convert the document.

The owner might also have set usage restrictions on the document. You can find restrictions of the current document in . PdfToSvg.NET will honor export restrictions. If you are the author of the document you can bypass the usage restrictions by providing the owner password.

member.summary: Contains options affecting the behavior when a PDF page is converted to SVG.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.ImageResolver
member.summary: Gets or sets a class that is used to resolve URLs for images.
member.remarks: The default implementation embeds all images as data URLs. You can implement a resolver yourself to e.g. save the images to files and instead include URLs to the separate image files in the SVG markup.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.FontResolver
member.summary: Gets or sets an implementation that will be used for deciding what font to be used for text included in the SVG.

remarks.para: The default implementation will in first hand try to embed fonts as WOFF files, and if not possible, fallback to detecting standard fonts and assuming the client has those installed. You can implement a custom font resolver for e.g. using custom WOFF or WOFF2 files, or saving the embedded fonts as separate font files.

item.description: Extracts fonts from the PDF, converts them to OpenType format, and then embed them as data URLs in the SVG.
Extracts fonts from the PDF, converts them to WOFF format, and then embed them as data URLs in the SVG.
Tries to match the PDF fonts with commonly available fonts, and references them by name.

remarks.para: PDF documents store text encoded as character codes, and provide mappings from character codes to font glyphs and Unicode characters. Some documents map multiple character codes to the same Unicode character, giving PdfToSvg.NET a choice. Exporting both character codes as the same Unicode character results in good text representation but potentially visually inaccurate SVG’s. Remapping one of the character codes to another Unicode character ensures visually accurate SVG’s at the cost of inaccurate text representation if text is exported from the SVG.
When exporting text using FontResolver.LocalFonts, the library will use the Unicode mapping specified by the document, providing more accurate text representation.

When exporting text using FontResolver.EmbedOpenType or FontResolver.EmbedWoff, the library will remap duplicate character codes to characters in the Private Use Areas, making sure the exported SVG’s are visually accurate, but text might appear as a series of question marks, ������, in the SVG markup. If you intend to extract text from the SVG, consider exporting the SVG using local fonts instead.

example.para: The following example will use to convert a PDF to SVG without embedding fonts into the extracted SVG. Instead local fonts assumed to be installed on the client machine are used.

code.title: Using local fonts instead of embedding fonts

example.para: Custom behavior can be achieved by subclassing and implementing the method. Here is a custom implementation using a locally installed Open Sans font.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.MinStrokeWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum stroke width that will be used in the resulting SVG. If the PDF use a thinner stroke width, it will be replaced with this width. The default value is 0.5.

remarks.para: The value is expressed in transformed user space units of the converted PDF page. By default 1 user space unit is 1/72 inch (0.35 mm), but this can be overridden by the PDF document. Transforms can affect the actual minimum width in the generated SVG.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.CollapseSpaceLocalFont
member.summary: Explicit spacing between letters below this threshold will be removed and merged to a single text span when using a local font. The default value is 0.2.

remarks.para: The value is relative to the current font size, where 1.0 represents the font size. This property affects text using a local font. A high value produces long text spans. This is better for local fonts, where the actual font metrics might not match the metrics of the original font.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.CollapseSpaceEmbeddedFont
member.summary: Explicit spacing between letters below this threshold will be removed and merged to a single text span when using an embedded font. The default value is 0.02.

remarks.para: The value is relative to the current font size, where 1.0 represents the font size. This property affects text formatted with an embedded font. Text inlined as paths is not affected. A low value produces a more accurate result, while a high value produces a more compact SVG markup.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.IncludeLinks
member.summary: Determines whether web links from the PDF document will be included in the generated SVG. The default value is true.

remarks.para: Note that this property only affects links to websites. Other types of links, including links within the document, are currently not supported.

example.para: The following example will exclude links from the generated SVG. This might be good if you don't want the SVG to lead the user away from the document.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.IncludeAnnotations
member.summary: Determines whether annotations drawn in the PDF document should be included in the generated SVG. The default value is true.

remarks.para: Interactive annotations are not supported. Links are technically also annotations, but are configured by the property.

Annotations are inserted as <g> elements, decorated with metadata attributes in the namespace https://pdftosvg.net/xmlns/annotations. Note that some annotations are only visible either in print or on screen.
remarks.code: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:annot="https://pdftosvg.net/xmlns/annotations"> <g annot:type="Text" annot:created="2024-02-18T12:37:31+01:00" annot:popup-title="John Smith" annot:popup-contents="Typo, should be 'than', not 'then'."> <path d="M100 100v2h2v-2z" fill="#000" /> </g> </svg>
remarks.para: PdfToSvg.NET may use the following attributes:

item.description: Specifies the type of annotation. A list of possible types can be found in Table 169 in the PDF 1.7 spec.

Some annotations have information that will appear in a popup when the document is opened in a PDF viewer. This attribute contains the text that would appear as title of this popup. The author of the annotation is usually specified as title.
Text comment that would appear as content of the popup.
Time when the annotation was added to the PDF document.

If the annotation refers to a file, this attribute specifies the file index in the collection on the owner page. The data is not included in the generated SVG but must be extracted and handled separately using .

example.para: The following example will exclude annotations from the generated SVG.

member.name: P:PdfToSvg.SvgConversionOptions.IncludeHiddenText
member.summary: Determines whether hidden text from the PDF document will be included in the generated SVG. The default value is true.

remarks.para: Hidden text is used for multiple purposes in PDF documents. Some examples:

list.item: For making it possible to search for and select text that is otherwise presented as an image. This is common in scanned documents processed with OCR (optical character recognition).
For embedding hidden metadata about the file, e.g., the name of the software producing the document.
For clipping other graphics to the text outline.

remarks.para: By setting this property to false, PdfToSvg.NET will generate smaller SVG files for some PDF documents, but it will have no or minimal impact on most documents.

Setting the property to false does not remove text used for clipping, since it is required for preserving the appearance of the page. It does however remove duplicated <text> nodes otherwise generated for making the clipping text searchable and selectable.

example.para: The following example will exclude hidden from the generated SVG markup. This will in some cases result in smaller SVG files.

code.title: Exclude hidden text in generated SVG
